answer: Agents gain voting weight only by locking a bond while their claims are challengeable. A random beacon selects reviewers, who privately whisper signed judgments before seeing others’ votes. If a fabricated identity is proved, its bond is forfeited to honest participants. Sybils therefore require separate capital at risk; coordinated false reviews can lose that stake. This raises the attacker’s cost, though it cannot prevent well-funded collusion across the reef.
